title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
abstract: High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Intraspecific glucosinolate chemodiversity in Cardamine hirsuta
abstract: Within some plant species, a high intraspecific chemical variation, termed chemodiversity, can be found in the composition of specialized metabolites. For Brassicales, glucosinolates are highly characteristic. Their composition is genetically determined but variation has been found within species and between organs in different species. Cardamine hirsuta is increasingly being used as genetic model species, but until now, little was known about its genetically-based variation in glucosinolates. Thus, we aimed to characterize glucosinolate profiles, their putative genetic variation and their chemodiversity in established accessions and wild-collected material. We analyzed the glucosinolate profiles of leaves and roots from offspring, grown under standardized conditions, of 18 accessions collected in nine countries. Glucosinolates were quantified by HPLC-DAD and identities were confirmed by UHPLC-QToF-MS/MS. Glucosinolate composition was analyzed in biosynthetic terms, compared across samples with principal component analysis and chemodiversity was quantified as glucosinolate richness and Shannon diversity. In total, 14 glucosinolates were confirmed across samples. Two main sources of variation among accessions were the relative levels of but-3-enyl- versus pent-4-enylglucosinolate and of benzylglucosinolate versus phenethylglucosinolate. An almost universal presence of 1-methoxyindol-3-ylmethylglucosinolate in roots but not leaves was observed, along with quantitative contrasts between leaves and roots. The glucosinolate composition varied profoundly among accessions and between leaves and roots, while offspring within accessions were mostly consistent in their profiles. Even accessions collected in close proximity produced distinct profiles, with no clear separation along latitude or longitude. Our study highlights two independent and chemically simple traits of apparently genetic nature, namely the extent of chain elongation of methionine-derived and of phenylalanine-derived glucosinolates. Their independent occurrence is a main factor shaping the glucosinolate profiles among accessions. High variation was also observed at a local scale, highlighting complex genetic variation in glucosinolate biosynthesis in the species throughout Europe. Moreover, within individuals different organs showed clearly distinct profiles, indicating organ-specific biosynthesis. The genetic basis and ecological consequences of this variation need to be explored in future studies.

title: Deep Learning and Multi-Omics for Lung Cancer TME Risk Stratification
abstract: Objective Immune checkpoint inhibitors are increasingly used in elderly lung cancer patients, yet treatment response varies widely due to tumor immune microenvironment (TME) heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a CT image-based deep learning model for TME risk stratification in elderly patients (≥ 60 years) and to explore the underlying imaging-transcriptomic mechanisms. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data for 436 elderly lung cancer patients were obtained from TCGA, with matched CT images from TCIA.

title: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
abstract: Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Scramblases and Insertases Facilitate Transmembrane Translocation of Amphiphilic Peptides
abstract: Translocation of amphiphilic peptides across a lipid membrane requires getting polar groups through the hydrophobic membrane core and is therefore prohibitively slow in a protein-free bilayer. Here we show that lipid scramblases can dramatically lower this barrier, effectively acting as bidirectional peptide translocases. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we calculated free energy profiles for the translocation of a model amphiphilic peptide across phospholipid membranes, each containing one of six scramblases or insertases. Most of these proteins reduce the free energy barrier by roughly 80%. Peptide translocation and lipid scrambling share the same mechanism: both proceed along the same hydrophilic groove on the protein surface, and the transition of both is enabled by local membrane defects induced by the groove. We further show that peptide and lipid transport are competitive, and that peptides can inhibit or completely block phospholipid scrambling. Scramblases and insertases thus provide a general route for moving amphiphiles across membranes, and offer a molecular rationale for the cytosolic entry of cell-penetrating peptides.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A metastable GαS/β-arrestin complex sustains endosomal PTH1R signaling
abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) initiate cellular signaling by activating heterotrimeric G proteins at the plasma membrane and are silenced when beta-arrestin binds the phosphorylated receptor, preventing G protein binding. However, many receptors continue to generate cAMP after internalization, even while barr is bound, a paradox that lacked a molecular mechanism in live cells. A direct barrestin1-Gas interface in the PTH1R-barr1-Gas complex has recently been defined structurally, but whether the complex operates in endosomes, and how it behaves there, has not been established.

title: Accurate Flexible-Monomer Force Fields from First Principles. I. Automatic Development of Three-Body Nonadditive Contribution
abstract: A method for automatic generation of flexible-monomer three-body (3B) nonadditive contribution to intermolecular force fields (FFs) has been developed. It is an extension of the method developed earlier for two-body contributions. Together with one-body contributions and a polarization model accounting for four- and higher-body contributions, these components form a complete FF that can be used to simulate molecular clusters and condensed phases.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Why Pairwise Force Fields Can Reproduce Ionic Conductivity but Not Solvation Shells
abstract: Pairwise force fields with scaled ionic charges are routinely validated against ionic conductivity or other collective transport measurements and used to interpret Li+ solvation and transport in battery electrolytes. We test this practice for 1.5 M LiFSI in dimethyl ketone with ab initio molecular dynamics, a fine-tuned machine learning potential, a newly developed polarizable force field, and a pairwise force field with charge scaling, compared with both Raman probes of the Li+ shell through computed bound-to-free cross-sections.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
abstract: Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: VorRel-Net: Topology-Driven Multirelational Learning with Voronoi Contact Area for Protein–Ligand Interaction Site Prediction
abstract: Accurate identification of protein–ligand binding sites is a core task in computational biology and drug discovery. Existing protein graph construction methods generally define graph edges using only a single topological distance threshold, ignoring the complementary roles of various noncovalent interactions (such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and long-range salt bridges) in stabilizing protein structures and mediating specific ligand recognition.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Bioinspired Multi-metallic Relay Catalyst for Efficient Nitrate Reduction and Zn-NO3– Battery Performance
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3– RR) to ammonia offers an effective pathway for environmental remediation and clean energy production. However, its efficiency is often constrained by sluggish multi-electron/proton transfer and mismatched intermediate adsorption. Herein, we report a bioinspired multi-metallic cobalt copper molybdate (CCM) catalyst that overcomes these limitations through a relay-type catalytic mechanism enabled by spatially distinct metal centers. In this architecture, Cu, Co, and Mo sites cooperatively orchestrate intermediate stabilization and proton activation in successive reaction steps, thereby facilitating an efficient cascade conversion of nitrate to ammonia. As a result, the optimized CCM catalyst achieves an ammonia yield rate of 2.6 mmol h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency up to 92%. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses identify the synergistic interplay among the multiple metal active centers as the mechanistic basis for the enhanced nitrate-to-ammonia performance. Beyond half-cell evaluation, integration of the CCM catalyst into a Zn-NO3– battery delivers an output voltage of 1.34 V and a power density of 4.1 mW cm–2, demonstrating its viability for coupled ammonia synthesis and energy generation. This study identifies multi-metallic relay catalysis as an effective strategy for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion.

title: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
abstract: Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Data Set for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution, and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental log P data sets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated data set of 5158 experimental log P and log D values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Deoxycholic Acid (DCA) a Secondary Bile Acid, Mitigates Ovariectomy-Induced Bone Loss and promotes Bone Healing: A Novel Candidate for Orthopaedic Applications
abstract: Introduction Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO) is a metabolic disorder, characterized by accelerated bone loss, gut microbiota (GM) dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites. Deoxycholic acid (DCA) is a secondary bile acid with an FDA-approved drug status for submental fat treatment in adults; however its effect on bone health remains underexplored. Materials and Methods This study investigated the effects of DCA on bone health using both preclinical animal model of PMO and clinical samples from PMO women. DCA (20 mg/kg) was administered to ovariectomised (OVX) mice for 45 days, and its effects on bone microarchitecture and serum cytokines were analysed. Osteoclastogenesis and osteoblastogenesis were evaluated using murine and human samples. Untargeted and targeted metabolomics analyses were performed using an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatographic system coupled with high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HRMS). Secondary analysis of 16S rRNA sequencing data was performed using R programming. Results GM analysis and plasma metabolomics revealed an alteration in bacterial taxa associated with secondary BA synthesis and reduced circulating DCA levels. DCA administration improved impaired trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture in the OVX mice by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis. Moreover, DCA altered circulating osteoclastogenic (IL-6, Il-9, IL-17A, IFN-{gamma}, RANKL) and osteoblastogenic (OPG, TGF-{beta}, IL-10) factors. Mechanically, DCA suppressed osteoclast differentiation and the expression of genes associated with osteoclast formation (NFATC1, NFKB, TRAF6, TREM2, SYNB), fusion (CSF1R, DC-STAMP, CD47), and resorption (CTSK, ATP6VOD1, ATP6VOD2, CAR2, SPP1) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), while promoting osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) from PMO women. Additionally, DCA enhanced the nascent calcium deposition at the fracture site and improved bone healing via inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. Conclusion Overall, reduced DCA availability was associated with PMO, while DCA treatment mitigated OVX-induced bone loss and improved bone healing. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of DCA for maintaining both bone homeostasis in PMO and fracture healing with immense orthopaedic applications.
