Using AI to predict how bioplastics behave under heat
abstract: A new ANIPH study shows how machine learning models can predict how PHB and PHBV respond to heat, helping manufacturers design formulations that are easier to process.

title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
abstract: The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: From Chemical Complexity to Magnetic Tunability in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
abstract: High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Computational Insights into How Structural Changes in the Hydrophobic Region of ALS-Linked Mutant SOD1 (G93A) Activate Fluctuations of the Electrostatic Loop: Implications for Aggregation
abstract: Cu/Zn-superoxide dismutase (SOD1) is an essential antioxidant enzyme that converts superoxide radicals into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. On the other hand, mutations in SOD1 cause familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (fALS), and these mutant forms tend to aggregate. Our previous research has shown that residue I35, located in a hydrophobic region, plays a critical role in the intracellular aggregation of SOD1. Furthermore, introducing an additional I35S mutation suppressed aggregate formation and eye degeneration in a Drosophila model caused by ALS-linked mutant SOD1.

title: Benchmarking Nonpolarizable Mg2+ Parameters Reveals Trade-Offs in RNA Conformational Sampling
abstract: In molecular dynamics simulations of RNA, Mg2+ ion force field parameters remain highly sensitive to the choice of water model and nucleic acid force field. The choice of Mg2+ force field parameters requires intentional thought, and although recent trends in nucleic acid force field development increasingly use the OPC water model, the compatibility of Mg2+ parameters with the OL3/OPC combination is insufficiently characterized. Here, we benchmark a panel of Mg2+ force fields: first in water boxes containing OPC with a single Mg2+ ion, and then in simulations with the Varkud satellite ribozyme stem loop V (SLV) as a model RNA, using the OL3 force field with LJbb corrections (OL3-LJbb). While most Mg2+ models are designed to reproduce the experimental ordering of hydration shells, they still differ substantially in diffusion coefficients and hydration free energies, reflecting the known trade-off between reproducing hydration thermodynamics and ion-oxygen distances in divalent-cation parametrization. These differences translate directly to RNA simulations, where Mg2+ models with slower diffusion and overly favorable hydration free energies promote long time-scale RNA binding events (“chelation”) and disrupt Mg2+-driven conformational changes. Together, these results highlight the need to validate divalent ion parameters specifically within the water model and RNA force field environment used for production-phase RNA molecular simulations, as well as demonstrate the Varkud satellite ribozyme as a sensitive benchmark for Mg2+/RNA/solvent force field compatibility.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: A systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures
abstract: MotivationEnzymes catalyse most of the metabolic reactions in living organisms. The functional characterization of enzymes is critical to understand the metabolic processes involved in different fields such as biotechnology, nutrition, ecology, and drug development. The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers provide a hierarchical framework for classifying enzymatic reactions, linking gene and protein sequences to biochemical transformations.

title: Rh₃ clusters balance activity and butene selectivity in butane dehydrogenation
abstract: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with researchers from Peking University and Chongqing University, have demonstrated how the geometry and electronic properties of subnanometer rhodium (Rh) active sites shape C–H activation, product desorption and C–C bond cleavage during butane dehydrogenation.

title: FrictionSim2D: A High-Throughput Molecular Simulation Framework to Screen the Friction of Two-Dimensional Materials
DNA Sequence Differentially Modulates Histone Core and Tail Interactions in Canonical and Centromeric Nucleosomes
abstract: Human centromeric chromatin is a specialized chromatin domain characterized by CENP-A-containing nucleosomes interspersed with canonical histone H3 nucleosomes. It is assembled on tandem repeats of -satellite DNA and defines centromere identity. How histone variant identity and DNA sequence jointly shape nucleosome structure and histone-DNA interactions that underpin centromeric chromatin formation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the structural plasticity of the histone core and nucleosomal DNA, histone tail dynamics and DNA-sequence dependent changes for canonical (H3) and centromeric (CENP-A) nucleosomes using the SIRAH coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) simulations. Nucleosomes containing -satellite positioning sequence (ASP) and Widom 601 DNA sequence are systematically analyzed and compared. Our simulations reveal that the centromeric nucleosome exhibits a more stable histone core with lower structural plasticity and the histone tails engage DNA differently with an overall reduction in the histone-DNA contacts compared to the canonical nucleosome. Further investigation of CENP-N binding to the CENP-A nucleosome demonstrates substantial modulation of nucleosomal DNA dynamics and histone-DNA interactions. Replacing the ASP DNA sequence with the Widom 601 sequence preserves the stability of both types of the histone core while markedly altering histone-tail dynamics. The conformational dynamics of canonical nucleosomes is more strongly affected by the Widom 601 DNA sequence than those of their centromeric counterparts. However, CENP-N binding induces more spatially extensive changes in DNA geometry in Widom 601 than in ASP DNA. Our findings suggest that DNA sequence and histone composition have residue-level differences translating into distinct nucleosome dynamics, which could be among the determinants governing the structural and dynamic properties of centromeric chromatin and its biological function.

title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
abstract: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
abstract: Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide…

title: Molecular Insights into the Allosteric Regulation of Pyruvate Kinase in Streptococcus pneumoniae
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a clinically important fermentative pathogen that relies heavily on glycolysis for energy production. Its rate-limiting enzyme, pyruvate kinase (SpPYK), is allosterically activated by the effector fructose-1,6-bisphosphate that binds ∼40 Å away from the substrate-binding catalytic site; however, the dynamic mechanism driving this long-range communication remains elusive. In this study, we employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and network analysis to map the allosteric activation pathway of SpPYK. Our results indicate that effector binding reshapes the dynamical landscape of the protein, increasing the coherence of collective motions coupled to active-site activation and rewiring long-range correlations. Our computational findings were validated by mutagenesis assays, which confirmed the role of key leucine residues within the activation pathway for the catalytic activity of the enzyme. Our findings refine the “Rock and Lock” model of allostery and offer a structural blueprint for leveraging allosteric regulation to develop species-selective antimicrobials.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
abstract: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024.

title: Learning the limits of protein structure models with NMR chemical shifts
abstract: Protein foundation models are intended to implicitly learn the chemical rules underlying protein function. However, systematically evaluating what biochemistry these models have learned remains difficult, as most downstream tasks lack experimental data fine-grained enough to expose their failure modes. NMR chemical shifts fill this gap: as direct per-atom reporters of local chemical environment, they offer a sensitive probe of structure-based representations. In this work, we present a systematically curated chemical shift dataset designed to minimize experimental confounders. We use it to benchmark diverse protein foundation models in their ability to predict backbone 15N chemical shifts, atoms that are known to be sensitive to many effects. The largest error across all models is in core residues with evidence of fast-timescale dynamics, which we investigate mechanistically using molecular dynamics simulations. Given the biological relevance of structured dynamic regions, we trained a new model based on the best of these embeddings, SLAE, to predict its own error. SLAE-ERR achieves a mean absolute error of 0.76 ppm for predicting error. Together, we hope that the datasets, evaluation tasks, and models presented here are sources of guidance for protein design model improvement.

title: A unique sixth-order reversible assembly of hexameric mimetic nucleic acid
abstract: Complementary dipeptides bearing the non-canonical nucleobases melamine and cyanuric acid (alpha DPNA) assemble into a cylindrical hexameric structure containing a stacked heterocyclic core with its beta-sheet peptide backbones on the surface. Circular dichroism spectroscopy and singular-value decomposition show that the evolution of CD spectra after mixing equimolar strands is an apparent two-state process, accounted for by only the spectra of free strands and the assembled hexamer, with no detectable intermediates.

title: Proteomic Evaluation of the Progression from Acute Kidney Injury to Chronic Kidney Disease
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are interconnected syndromes with substantial global burden, yet the molecular mechanisms driving the transition from acute injury to chronic fibrosis remain incompletely understood. We performed quantitative data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) proteomics on mouse models of AKI (ischemia-reperfusion injury) and CKD (unilateral ureteral obstruction), quantifying 5,985 protein groups.

title: Tailoring Surface Defects in SBA-15 Via Heteroatom Distortion for Enhanced CO2-to-Methanol Yield
abstract: The conversion of CO2 to methanol presents a viable energy solution that mitigates greenhouse gas emissions by utilizing CO2 to produce fuel. In this work, the inert mesoporous silica material SBA-15 was strategically fine-tuned to serve as an active support by incorporating Ti into its framework, followed by the impregnation of CuNiGa into it, which enhances electron transfer between the constituent metals. This modification results in the formation of a Cu1.5Ni1.5Ga ternary alloy phase, which activates CO2 and facilitates H2 spillover.

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function
abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs.
venue: Journal of computational biology : a journal of computational molecular cell biology

title: Electronic and Thermal Properties of Crystalline and Polycrystalline Ni3S2: A Metal with Weak Grain Boundaries Contribution
abstract: Ni3S2 is a metallic nickel sulfide with promising catalytic properties, yet its transport behavior remains poorly investigated. In this work, we synthesize single-crystalline (via CVT) and densified (via SPS) polycrystalline Ni3S2 samples and characterize their electronic and thermal properties over a broad temperature range, extending up to 700 K for the polycrystalline material.

title: Authenticity identification of wasabi (Eutrema wasabi) and its analogues by integrated genomic, barcoding-machine learning, and nutritional analysis
abstract: Wasabi's high market value drives its adulteration with taxonomically related analogues, compromising food quality and safety. We developed an integrated approach combining chloroplast genome comparison, DNA barcoding with machine learning classifiers, and nutritional profiling to distinguish wasabi from adulterants. Among seven Brassicaceae species, chloroplast genomes were largely conserved but exhibited species-specific variations in IR boundaries, SSRs, hypervariable regions, and weak A/U-ended codon bias.

title: Functional Cooperation between Pt Single Atoms and Nanoparticles on TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation and C–C Coupling
abstract: Dehydrogenative coupling reactions that activate inert C–H bonds for C–C bond formation remain challenging because of unfavorable thermodynamics and kinetics without external oxidants. We report a hybrid photocatalytic system consisting of mixed Pt species on TiO2 (Ptmix/TiO2) combined with the hydrogen atom transfer reagent 2,2,2-trichloroethanol (TCE) for the dehydrogenative coupling of toluene. The system delivers 11% toluene conversion with 94% selectivity to bibenzyl and stoichiometric H2 evolution.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Critical Assessments of Computational Hit-finding Experiments Challenge #4: Targeting the Tyrosine Kinase Binding Domain of the E3 Ligase Casitas B-Lineage Lymphoma Proto-Oncogene B, an Immuno-Oncology Target
abstract: The critical assessments of computational hit-finding experiments (CACHE) are prospective benchmarking exercises where small molecule ligands predicted for a nominated protein of interest are procured and tested experimentally. In CACHE #4, 23 participating teams each selected up to 100 compounds designed to bind the E3 ligase CBLB, an immuno-oncology target. The organizers released the first public structure of CBLB in complex with a known ligand at the outset of the challenge to enable the discovery of chemically novel molecules.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Molecular sensor makes invisible traces of mercury easier to see
abstract: Mercury contamination presents an obvious challenge: it is invisible. A glass of water or a piece of fruit can seem perfectly normal to the naked eye, even when trace amounts of toxic mercury are present. Detecting such minute levels usually requires specialized laboratory tools and trained experts.

title: High-Performance All-Atom Continuous Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics and Native Asynchronous Replica Exchange in Amber
abstract: Conformational dynamics of biomolecules, including proteins and nucleic acids, are often coupled to changes in protonation states. All-atom particle-mesh Ewald continuous constant-pH molecular dynamics (PME-CpHMD) enables proton-coupled dynamics, but its routine use has been limited by computational cost. Here we report a second-generation CUDA implementation of PME-CpHMD in Amber, in which the CpHMD-specific nonbonded corrections are evaluated in a separate kernel. Across protein systems ranging from 45 to 1,338 residues, the new implementation increases throughput by 1.5-2 fold relative to the previous fused-kernel implementation and limits the overhead relative to conventional MD to 12-18%. We also implemented the asynchronous pH replica-exchange (pH-REX) algorithm natively in pmemd.cuda.MPI, allowing simulations to run on fewer GPUs than replicas without the overhead of the previous Python wrapper. Furthermore, we derived CpHMD titration parameters for all six titratable residue types (Asp, Glu, His, Cys, Tyr, and Lys) for use with three protein force fields: CHARMM c22/CMAP, Amber ff14sb and ff19sb. The new implementations and parameterization were validated using pKa calculations of model peptides and hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL). The HEWL simulations revealed force-field-specific limitations, including overestimation of the pKa downshift 20 of H15 and sensitivity of the proton donor assignment in coupled E35/D52 dyad. Comparison with our previous work and the PME-CpHMD simulations in GROMACS with the CHARMM c36m force field demonstrated the robustness and sampling efficiency of pH-REX PME-CpHMD simulations. The new implementation provides a foundation for routine all-atom constant-pH simulations in Amber. The analysis highlights the need for continued development of protein force fields to more accurately balance intramolecular electrostatics and solvation of charged residues.

title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
abstract: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

title: Chromosome-level genomics and cross-species enzyme screening enable high-titer bakuchiol production in Yarrowia lipolytica
abstract: The diversity of enzymes supporting bakuchiol biosynthesis remains incompletely characterized, limiting the repertoire available for microbial pathway engineering. Here, we combined chromosome-level genomics, cross-species enzyme screening and metabolic engineering to establish high-titer bakuchiol production in Yarrowia lipolytica. We assembled a 471.76-Mb Psoralea corylifolia genome anchored to 11 pseudochromosomes, with a contig N50 of 40.33 Mb. Genome-guided screening and functional validation identified four prenyltransferases from P. corylifolia and Vigna radiata whose N-terminally truncated variants supported bakuchiol production in yeast. These results extend experimental evidence for bakuchiol-producing activity across legume prenyltransferase sequences and species. For PcPT6, corresponding to the previously reported PcPT07, removing 40 N-terminal amino acids increased bakuchiol production by 53% relative to the full-length enzyme. We reconstructed bakuchiol biosynthesis in Y. lipolytica and reinforced aromatic precursor synthesis to increase p-coumaric acid supply. Coordinating mevalonate pathway reinforcement with increased t40PcPT6 gene dosage further improved bakuchiol production. Following fermentation optimization, titers reached 108.29 mg/L in shake flasks and 6.03 g/L in a 7.5-L fed-batch bioreactor. These findings connect an expanded set of functional prenyltransferases with coordinated pathway engineering, enabling gram-per-liter microbial bakuchiol production.

title: Expanding Plasma Proteome Coverage While Preserving Biological Signatures: A Systematic Characterization of Enrichment and Preanalytical Variables
abstract: Plasma is a rich and accessible source for biomarkers. The analytical challenge of the steep dynamic range was recently addressed using enrichment technologies. Enrichment technologies have been shown to be sensitive to preanalytical variables, making this an active area of research. We established the P2 enrichment system as high-performing and robust for large scale studies, with reproducible identifications and precision across batches, days, operators and laboratories. We characterized P2-based enrichment for preanalytical variables (eight blood collection types, centrifugation, freeze-thaw and pathogen inactivation). K2EDTA-plasma resulted in the deepest proteome coverage with about 6000 protein groups on the timsTOF HT. We spiked 16 heavy-labelled proteins into platelet-poor and platelet-contaminated plasma. Importantly, linearity, accuracy, and precision were high in both platelet-poor and platelet-contaminated plasma for both P2-enriched and neat preparations. In a cancer cohort, we demonstrated that 97% of differentially abundant proteins retained the same direction of regulation after P2-based enrichment compared with the neat preparation. Differentially abundant proteins identified in a colorectal cancer pilot cohort remained largely conserved after platelet contamination, including previously reported biomarkers. We demonstrated that P2-based enrichment enables deep, large scale proteome profiling and preserves biological information despite preanalytical variation. Candidates emerging from P2-based discovery can be validated in independent cohorts with targeted assays.

title: Lipid Scrambling Amplifies Plasma Membrane Undulations via Anti-Registered Domains Stabilized by Long-Chain Sphingomyelin
abstract: Lipid scrambling, which dissipates the transbilayer lipid asymmetry of plasma membranes (PMs), plays an essential role in various large-scale membrane remodeling processes. Although lipid domains have been implicated in these processes, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, owing to the lack of a molecular-level picture of how lipid scrambling reorganizes these domains. Here, using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of asymmetric and fully scrambled PM models, we show that lipid scrambling markedly enhances membrane undulations. We identify two key features of the domain organization underlying this enhancement in the scrambled PM: domain anti-registration, which couples to membrane curvature through a mismatch in preferred curvature between the two leaflets, and scrambling-induced domain enlargement, which permits this curvature to extend over large length scales. Simulations with different sphingomyelin (SM) compositions demonstrate that long-chain SMs stabilize anti-registered domains and the associated membrane curvature. Together, these results suggest a physical mechanism by which lipid scrambling primes the PM for remodeling through the reorganization of lipid domains, with long-chain SMs playing a key role. We also find that the interleaflet domain organization of the scrambled PM model depends strongly on system size, shifting from anti-registration to registration as the simulation box is reduced, and we discuss the origin of this finite-size effect.

title: Optimizing assay conditions for gaussia luciferase
abstract: Gaussia luciferase (GLuc) is a widely used reporter enzyme due to its small size and exceptionally intense light output. However, its characteristic 'flash' properties have made accurate determination of enzyme activity sensitive to minute variations in the experimental setup, which is the likely cause of many inconsistent and contradictory findings in the literature. The intrinsic instability of the substrate, coelenterazine, adds to these complications. Furthermore, at the high dilutions commonly required to measure this exceptionally active enzyme, the signal often deviates from the expected linear relationship between activity and concentration due to adsorption. In this study, we systematically investigated the critical experimental parameters that affect activity measurements using a 96-well plate reader with an automated injection system. To illustrate experimental issues, we applied our analysis to measurements of GLuc and GLuc variants with widely different levels of activity and decay rates as well as with different substrates. We demonstrate that variations in 1) latency between substrate injection and measurement, 2) enzyme dilution and adhesion, and 3) substrate handling and degradation can lead to inconsistent values for specific activity. Based on this, we suggest a framework for optimizing GLuc assay conditions for reproducibility.

title: Evaluating speech-like distortion product otoacoustic emissions: a comparison of time- and frequency-domain metrics across three datasets
abstract: Speech-like distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) allow cochlear activity to be measured during the perception of natural, continuous speech and have been used to study attentional effects in the cochlea. The technique is still young, however, and existing studies differ in stimulus design and in the metric used to quantify the emissions, which makes their results difficult to compare. Here, we reanalysed three existing datasets (106 participants, 14 stimulus types) with a common pipeline. We compared six metrics: the band power of the recording, the magnitude-squared coherence (MSC) between the recording and a DPOAE template, and four metrics derived from their complex cross-correlation, namely peak magnitude, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), peak area and peak width. A separability index quantified how well each metric separated in-ear recordings from out-of-ear control recordings without emissions. Band power, MSC and SNR separated best, with mean separability indices of about 0.9, whereas the peak magnitude performed worst and was inverted for half of the stimulus types. Since band power does not require a DPOAE template, it serves as a sanity check of the setup rather than as evidence for an emission. The MSC was insensitive to the latency of the emission but well suited for comparisons across stimuli, whereas the cross-correlation additionally provided the latency. The emissions differed significantly between the stimulus types of the three datasets, and those below about 700 Hz were measured least reliably. We derive practical recommendations for the analysis and stimulus design of future experiments.

title: Advancing AOPs for genotoxicity through quantifying KERs linking DNA alkylation to increase in mutations and chromosome aberrations
abstract: Quantitative Adverse Outcome Pathways (qAOPs) help translate mechanistic knowledge into quantitative toxicity predictions; however, their development is constrained by the limited availability and heterogeneity of quantitative data. Here, we investigated the feasibility of developing a qAOP for genotoxicity by modeling quantitative relationships linking DNA alkylation to increased mutations and structural chromosome aberrations through intermediate biological key events (KEs). We compiled and harmonized published concentration-response data from human lymphoblastoid TK6 cells exposed to ethyl methanesulfonate, methyl methanesulfonate, or N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea, covering eight genotoxicity assays representing five KEs with well-established dependencies. We evaluated sources of variability, compared points of departure (PoDs), and quantified relationships between successive events using response-response modeling. Substantial between-study variability could to a limited extent be explained through differences in experimental design while batch effects for individual studies and researchers were substantial. PoD estimates that were calculated from combined results of independent studies with similar experimental design, were often uncertain due to insufficient concentration-response characterization or conflicting results between studies. Nevertheless, response-response modeling suggested a threshold effect for certain key-event relationships (KERs). Specifically, DNA adducts seemed to be triggered at lower concentrations of alkylating agents compared to the subsequent KEs of DNA strand breaks and chromosome aberrations. Furthermore, these fitted response-response models can be used for prediction of downstream KEs from earlier ones. The general approach we developed for BMC analysis followed by response-response modeling is applicable to other AOPs as well. These findings highlight both the feasibility and limitations of using existing data for qAOP development.

title: Combining KA Oil Oxidation and O2 Reduction to H2O2 Enables Kinetically and Energetically Favored Adipic Acid Production Pathways
abstract: Adipic acid (AA), produced via oxidation of KA oil (a mixture of cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone), is a crucial monomer for nylon-6,6 synthesis. Electrochemical oxidation of KA oil eliminates the use of the nitric acid oxidant in the conventional process, offering a greener approach. However, electrochemical KA oil oxidation is slow; in particular, the 6e– oxidation of cyclohexanone to AA is sluggish, increasing electrical energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate that pairing KA oil oxidation with the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) mitigates energetic and kinetic limitations. By replacing the commonly used hydrogen evolution reaction with the ORR, the operating voltage is greatly reduced. More importantly, we discovered that H2O2 generated from the 2e– ORR can oxidize cyclohexanone to 6-hydroperoxyhexanoic acid (HPHA), a reaction not previously reported in the literature. HPHA can then be further electrochemically oxidized to AA with significantly faster kinetics than cyclohexanone, effectively eliminating the kinetic bottleneck of electrochemical cyclohexanone oxidation. This discovery enables a three-step pathway for AA production: electrochemical oxidation of cyclohexanol to cyclohexanone, chemical oxidation of cyclohexanone to HPHA by H2O2, and electrochemical oxidation of HPHA to AA. The selectivity and efficiency of each reaction, as well as those of the overall process, are investigated in detail.

title: Spin Exchange Enables Two-Electron TEMPO Catholytes for Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: High-energy-density neutral aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) require a transition from one-electron/one-electron and two-electron/one-electron configurations to fully two-electron-matched systems. This goal has remained unrealized because stable two-electron catholytes are lacking, and even the most promising TEMPO materials still undergo proton-induced irreversible piperidine ring opening, causing rapid capacity decay. Here we report a hydration-cage-induced spin-exchange strategy for stabilizing two-electron AcNH-NMe-TEMPO catholytes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A reversible YbbR-domain hinge switch senses extracellular pH to control bacterial cyclic-di-AMP signaling
abstract: Acidification is a principal antimicrobial host defence: during infection, bacteria have to survive the stomach, the vaginal tract or the phagolysosome of immune cells, where the pH falls below 5. To persist, bacteria must sense and adapt to extracellular pH. In Gram-positive bacteria, the membrane protein CdaR, a regulator of the c-di-AMP-synthesizing enzyme CdaA, has been proposed as a pH sensor, but the molecular basis of this sensing remains unknown. Here we show, using the model organism Bacillus subtilis, that CdaR is essential for growth below pH 5.

title: Overlap of competing voices may mask attentional effects on speech-like distortion product otoacoustic emissions
abstract: Whether selective auditory attention modulates the cochlear amplifier through the medial olivocochlear system remains debated. Using speech-like distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs), elicited by waveforms that follow the harmonics of natural speech, we previously found that selectively attending one of two competing talkers reduced the emissions related to the resolved harmonics of the female voice. Here, we attempted to reproduce this effect in a design that separated different frequency regimes and harmonic resolvability. Forty-four participants attended one of two competing talkers, a female and a male voice, presented to one ear, while speech-like DPOAEs related to both voices were recorded from the other ear. Stimuli were derived from resolved and unresolved harmonics in a low-frequency (up to 1.5 kHz) and a transitional (1.5 to 4 kHz) regime, which required pitch-shifting both voices so that their fundamental frequencies were much closer to each other than in the original study. Speech-like DPOAEs emerged for most stimulus types, although they were weak for some and absent for one. Their amplitude, however, did not depend on attention for any stimulus type. Further time-domain metrics showed only isolated attentional effects of opposite direction for two stimulus types, and a frequency-domain metric showed none. A cochlear excitation model suggests that, due to the closely spaced fundamental frequencies of the two voices, the emissions most comparable to the original study presumably arose at cochlear locations shared by both voices, where attention would modulate both voices alike.

title: Actin Assembly on Biomimetic Lipid-coated and Functionalized Bead Surfaces
abstract: Dynamic assembly of actin filaments drives cell protrusion and other aspects of cell motility. Reconstitution of actin assembly from purified components is a powerful approach for understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie these processes. Purified preparations of actin, actin-binding proteins, and regulators of actin-binding proteins enable a broad spectrum of reconstitution experiments. Much of this actin filament assembly occurs at the plasma membrane, with exquisite temporal and spatial regulation. We developed a biomimetic reconstitution system using purified lipids or glutathione on the surface of functionalized beads as models for actin assembly at the plasma membrane. The system incorporates two critical pathways for regulation of actin assembly: nucleation of actin polymerization by Arp2/3 complex and activation of heterodimeric actin capping protein (CP). Arp2/3 complex and CP are both essentially inactive in the basal resting state of the cytoplasm. The system incorporates membrane-bound activators for Arp2/3 complex, such as WASP and WAVE family proteins, and for CP, such as CARMILs and other CPI-motif proteins. Membrane-bound components are coupled to beads either through lipids, which allow lateral mobility, or through glutathione groups attached to the bead surface via flexible linkers. Fluorescence microscopy of labeled components, combined with quantitative image analysis, is used to assess the combined effects of the regulators and thereby test molecular mechanisms for regulation of actin assembly. Here, we describe protocols for preparing functionalized beads, coupling regulators to the bead surface, performing actin assembly reactions, and imaging and quantifying the resulting actin networks.

title: Binary Patterning as a Probe of Protein Language Model Representations
abstract: Do protein language models (pLMs) encode the physical rules that govern protein folding? The four-helix bundle provides a classic test case because binary patterning, the ordered placement of polar and nonpolar residues along an amphipathic -helix, is sufficient to generate folded proteins with high probability. Here, we ask whether ESM2 captures the sequence grammar underlying this design strategy. Libraries of synthetic sequences constrained only by binary patterning were predicted by ESMFold to form four-helix bundles. Predicted helicity, compactness, and topological diversity changed with sequence length in the same direction as experimentally characterized libraries, although the model did not distinguish successful from unsuccessful individual designs. Principal component analysis of ESM2 embeddings revealed representations of hydrophobic patterning, helix-loop boundaries, and heptad register. Extending the analysis to all 128 heptad binary patterns produced a jellyfish-shaped manifold in which hydrophobic composition formed the dominant axis, while paired components encoded pattern phase. Manifold geometry depended on amino-acid chemistry, repeat number, and linker sequence, and collapsed when amino acids were assigned to arbitrary categories. ESM2 therefore combines general repeat recognition with protein-specific physicochemical information. More broadly, synthetic sequence libraries provide experimentally grounded probes of protein language model representations and their relationship to protein biophysics.

title: Cochlear wave dispersion reveals partition micromechanics
abstract: Cochlear traveling waves are a fundamental aspect of mammalian hearing, enabling frequency selectivity. However, incorporating micromechanical interactions between the cells, membranes, and fluids that comprise the cochlear partition presents a challenge when accounting for this selectivity and other macro-scale response properties. The traveling wave can be characterized by its dispersion, which is the relationship between its wavenumber and frequency. One objective was to investigate how organ of Corti structural components influence wave dispersion. To achieve this, we adapted a conventional three-dimensional tapered cochlear box model by incrementally adding morphological characteristics that constitute the partition. Initially a flexible plate, the partition transformed to incorporate a tectorial membrane and inner spiral sulcus. Our secondary objective was to predict the dispersion for each variation using a reduced-length model (slice model). We observed that stiffness and the optimal frequency increased across variations, while wave dispersion remained unchanged relative to the optimal frequency. We also discovered that eigenfrequency analysis, using Floquet boundary conditions, accurately predicted the dispersion for each variation and revealed the existence of other propagating waves including a tectorial membrane transverse mode. These results underscore the significance of analyzing cochlear wave propagation from capturing macromechanical response properties thereby facilitating investigations of micromechanical interactions in reduced-length models.

title: Multiscale Drug–Cell Interaction Modeling via Hybrid Graph Architectures and Knowledge-Aware Fusion for Drug Synergy Prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug combination synergy remains challenging due to the vast combinatorial space and strong cellular context dependency of drug responses. To address these limitations, we present MILSyn, a multimodal interaction learning framework designed to capture multiscale drug–cell interactions through three integrated components: (1) relational modeling of heterogeneous graph structures using a hybrid RGCN-GATv2 architecture, (2) cross-modal fusion of biochemical features spanning SMILES, substructures, 3D conformations, and multiomic profiles, and (3) knowledge-aware reasoning…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Two-Step Photon Absorption in an Expanded Perovskite Analog with a Molecular Intermediate Band
abstract: Intermediate-band solar cells (IBSCs) introduce an intermediate band (IB) within the absorber’s band gap, allowing consecutive sub-band-gap two-step photon absorption (TSPA) to supplement band-gap absorption, enabling a 50% increase in the fundamental device efficiency limit. Current IBSC absorbers, however, introduce the IB as impurities in trace concentrations, affording weak sub-band-gap absorption. We demonstrate a novel material design for TSPA using (dmpz)Pb2I6 (dmpz2+ = N,N′-dimethylpyrazinium) containing a molecular IB. Notably, the organic–inorganic hybridization evident in electronic structure calculations, where electronic states from the iodide appear in the dmpz-based bands, and large thermal fluctuations revealed by molecular dynamics trajectories enhance subgap absorption at 300 K. Transient electronic signatures of photoreduced dmpz•+ radicals verify the charge-transfer nature of the sub-band-gap absorption, whereas coherent high-frequency vibrations reveal vibronic coupling between dmpz and the inorganic framework. Proof-of-concept solar cells with (dmpz)Pb2I6 generate increased photocurrent upon subgap IR excitation and display quadratic-to-linear power dependence. This first demonstration of TSPA with an intrinsic organic IB offers a new material class for IBSCs.

title: Combining five metals in one oxide improves ethanol gas sensing
abstract: A technology that significantly improves ethanol gas sensing performance by combining five different metal elements in a single oxide has been developed.

title: Water-activated polymer forms solid shapes underwater and bonds glass fragments
abstract: Cement hardens when mixed with water, allowing it to form solid structures even in wet environments. This property is known as hydraulicity. Reproducing this property in organic polymers has been challenging, as polymer materials that react with moisture often lack the combination of bulk curing and water resistance needed to harden reliably in wet conditions.

title: Interfacial Organization and Direction-Dependent Transport of Hydrocarbons in Graphene Slit Pores
abstract: Hydrocarbon transport in nanopores depends on the spatial organization of the confined fluid. We investigate this relationship through molecular dynamics simulations of methane, benzene, and n-octane between fixed graphene sheets, varying temperature and pore width. Density profiles and orientational distributions are combined with lateral mobility and wall-to-wall exchange to characterize structure and motion in interfacial and interior populations.

title: Understanding the Orchestrating Role of TLR2 in Differential Heterodimerization
EasyNMR: shareable flow-based workflows for reproducible analysis of NMR and other scientific data
abstract: Spectroscopic studies increasingly require analyses beyond what standard software offers, yet the programs that make them possible are often developed in single laboratories, are hard to maintain and are difficult to share. Here we present EasyNMR, a web-native platform that applies flow-based programming to the analysis of NMR spectra and other scientific data, turning each analysis into a shareable, executable workflow.

title: Comprehensive Two-dimensional liquid chromatography technology and its applications in the field of traditional Chinese medicine
abstract: Comprehensive two-dimensional liquid chromatography (LC×LC) represents a significant breakthrough in modern separation science. Theoretically, it leverages the synergistic effect of separation capabilities across both dimensions to substantially enhance peak capacity, providing robust technical support for analyzing complex systems such as traditional Chinese medicine. However, after nearly a decade of development and application, substantial gaps remain between its theoretical advantages and practical performance in TCM analysis.

title: Tautomerism and Diradical Character: Chemical and Electronic Structure of a High-Performance Organic Electrode Material
abstract: Bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) is a high-performance organic electrode material whose molecular structure remains a subject of debate, which we address in this joint experimentaltheoretical study. Using density functional theory (DFT) across multiple scales, from isolated molecules to periodic crystal structures, this work provides an atomistic insight into the structural and electronic complexity of TAQ.

title: Gain, Retention, or Loss of Aromaticity upon Surface Adsorption: π-Electron Systems on Cu(111)
abstract: Understanding the interactions between metal surfaces and the π-electron systems of flat-lying polycyclic conjugated hydrocarbons is central to designing metal–organic interfaces and on-surface synthesis. This surface interaction is sometimes rationalized in terms of aromaticity, which is usually evaluated for gas phase model systems and rarely for adsorbed molecules. Here, we use density functional theory to study changes in geometric and electronic aromaticity for 22 π-electron systems upon adsorption on Cu(111), from physisorption to strong chemisorption.

title: Bayesian Optimization Outperforms Experts for Spectral Model Development
abstract: Indirect Hard Modeling (IHM) is a physically motivated approach for quantitative spectral analysis that can account for nonlinear spectral changes, provides loweffort calibration, and allows extrapolation. However, realizing the full potential of IHM requires careful adjustment of model parameters and spectral preprocessing settings, which is typically performed manually and relies on expert knowledge. To address this limitation, we investigate Bayesian Optimization (BO) as a strategy for efficient IHM parameter tuning with mixed continuous, discrete, and categorical parameter spaces.

title: Donor priming and conformational control in arginine N-rhamnosylation by the glycosyltransferase EarP
abstract: EarP is an unusual glycosyltransferase that rhamnosylates R32 of bacterial elongation factor P (EF-P), catalyzing glycosylation of a poorly nucleophilic guanidinium moiety. How donor and acceptor are organized to enable this rare reaction remains incompletely understood. Here, we report the synthesis and use of complementary low-reactivity analogs of dTDP-rhamnose (dTDP-Rha) to capture structural states associated with substrate recognition and turnover by EarP from Neisseria meningitidis, supported by biochemical assays of glycosyl transfer.

title: synthmc: a precedent-based synthesizability score for transition metal complexes
abstract: Data-driven methods are increasingly being used for the in silico discovery of transition metal complexes (TMCs), ranging from machine learning models for high-throughput screening and generative models proposing new candidates to evolutionary algorithms for their de novo design. However, computationally discovered or designed TMCs are only rarely realized experimentally, in part because their synthesis is difficult and often not considered during the design process.

title: A mechanistic insight into the role of triplet states in excited-state deactivation of dibenzothiophene: a new fate for green chemistry
abstract: The environmental impact of petroleum derivatives is a current threat which needs to be studied and tackled in the present and near future. In this context, obtaining new insight about the degradation and remediation possibilities of polyaromatic sulphur heterocycles, and particularly dibenzothiophene, is a challenge requiring the full attention of the academic community. Thus, we have studied the dibenzothiophene excited state decay from a theoretical perspective, resorting to multiconfigurational methods, in order to obtain a full photophysical picture which until now was incomplete.

title: Linear-time Shape Alignment with ROSHAMBO3
abstract: Three-dimensional (shape) similarity is a useful primitive for virtual screening and molecular machine learning, but current open implementations are limited in performance by a quadratic inner loop across pairs of query-and databasemolecule atoms. ROSHAMBO3 achieves a 78–154× speedup over the previous open SOTA ROSHAMBO2 by using query-amortized Gaussian fields that make the inner loop linear combined with system-scale optimization at the algorithmic, GPU, and host layers, screening up to 55M query–conformer pairs/s on NVIDIA GPUs, with secondary CPU (x86, ARM) and Apple Metal backends.

title: Two-Step Recovery Kinetics with Distinct Time Scales in Stress-Softened Polyacrylamide-Carbon Nanotube Composite Hydrogels
abstract: Polyacrylamide-carbon nanotube (PAAm-CNT) composite hydrogels exhibit pronounced stress-softening alongside substantial CNT-induced toughening. Although stress-softening causes the reloading stress to drop significantly below the virgin loading stress, the underlying internal damage recovers given a sufficient resting period. We quantify the recovery dynamics using two independent metrics: the residual internal damage D R (defined as the hysteresis work loss) and the post-unloading residual strain ε R .

title: Ruthenium Catalyzed Reduction of N 2 O using MeOH as Hydrogen Source
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) is a significant contributor to climate change owing to its dual role as greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting molecule. Herein, the catalytic reduction of N 2 O to N 2 using methanol (MeOH) as a terminal reductant was investigated employing a series of Ru complexes supported by proton-responsive picoline- and lutidine-derived pincer ligands incorporating N-heterocyclic carbene donors (CNC and CNN).

title: Predicting the Fourth Analogue: Learning Stereochemical Transfer in Cyclic-Peptide Permeability
abstract: Combining stereochemical edits offers a direct way to explore cyclic-peptide chemical space. Once a reference peptide and two single-edit analogues have been measured, the modeling question is how molecular structure improves prediction beyond those three observations. We define this conditional permeability task using 1,154 chemically certified squares from four publications and evaluate transfer across 22 complete chemical families.

title: Metal-Free Spin Crossover Through Nitrogen-Intercalated Graphene Under Pressure
abstract: Spin crossover (SCO) phenomena, in which the spin state of an atom changes due to an external stimulus, have been the subject of ongoing research interest to this day. However, the considered atoms have been limited to transition metals like iron or cobalt. In this theoretical study, we show for the first time that external pressure can cause a nitrogen atom, i.e., a non-metal, to transit from a high spin (HS) to a low spin (LS) configuration.

title: AutoSPS-D2B: Automated Solid-Phase Synthesis Expands the Reaction Scope for Direct-to-Biology Libraries
abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) has emerged as a powerful accelerant in early drug discovery, bypassing compound purification to compress the design-make-test-analyse (DMTA) cycle. However, the chemistry underpinning D2B libraries is limited to just a few sequential transformations using assay-compatible reagents and solvents. By contrast, solid-phase synthesis (SPS) empowers a far broader range of reactions and is highly amenable to multistep synthesis, yet its potential as a source for D2B libraries remains largely underexplored.

title: Programmable Self-Sorting in Multi-Component Coordination Cage Systems via Ligand Tethering
abstract: Control over self-sorting in multi-component metal-organic self-assembly remains a major challenge as mixtures of ligands commonly yield statistical distributions of products. Integrative and heteromeric completive self-sorting regimes are both attractive non-statistical outcomes, but each typically requires system-specific design; switching between the two cannot readily be achieved within a single ligand set. Here, we show that a simple tethering strategy enables programmable self-sorting in heteroleptic Pd(II) coordination cages by chelation.

title: Microplastic Identification by Temperature-Resolved Fluorescence Imaging
abstract: Heating Nile Red-stained microplastics on a filter while imaging their fluorescence allows to determine their flowthrough temperatures, associated with melting or softening of the polymers. Using a widefield microscope and a consumer-grade camera we classify HDPE, LDPE, PP, PVC and PMMA by RGB values and flow-through temperature.

title: Structure Before Sequence: Physicochemical Catalytic Organization and Biological Reconstruction
abstract: Biological catalysis depends on highly organized protein and RNA architectures whose reproducible construction is itself sequence-supported, creating a familiar circularity in discussions of catalytic origins. This Perspective separates two questions that are often treated together: what physical organization is sufficient for catalytic function, and what sequencesupported biology adds to make selected catalytic architectures reproducibly reconstructable.

title: Light-induced signal enhancement in 13C solid-state NMR occurring in a flavin-tyrosine radical pair
abstract: “Light-oxygen-voltage” (LOV) domains are widespread flavin-containing proteins known for their numerous photosensory functions. Under illumination, some LOV domains form spin-correlated radical pairs (SCRPs), in which coherent spin evolution can lead to the buildup of transient nuclear hyperpolarization. In LOV domains, this solid-state photo-CIDNP (photochemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization) effect has so far been observed only with tryptophan as the electron donor. Here, we show that the effect can also be achieved with a tyrosine.

title: Complete Top-down Sequencing of Therapeutic Phosphorodiamidate Morpholino Oligomers by Multimodal Ion Activation in Both Polarities
abstract: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMOs) are an important class of approved antisense therapeutics whose neutral backbone presents significant challenges for tandem mass spectrometric sequencing. Here, we evaluate multiple ion activation strategies on a timsOmni™ prototype in both electrospray polarities using the approved PMO drugs viltolarsen (21-mer) and eteplirsen (30-mer).

title: A fluorescence polarization probe for rapid and quantitative analysis of interactions between Rubisco and small molecules
Physical consistency and completeness in the data-driven modeling of microwave absorbing materials
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been applied to the modeling of microwave absorbing materials, including the prediction of electromagnetic parameters and reflection loss (RL), yet the physical consistency of such models is rarely examined. This paper addresses two types of physical consistency problems in data-driven modeling: the physical inconsistency of predicted outputs and the physical incompleteness of input features. On the output side, we constructed a numerical integrator based on the Kramers-Kronig (KK) relation to test permittivity spectra output by ML models.

title: CadreAI: Agentic AI for Semantically Decoupled Protein–Drug Design and Optimization
abstract: De novo drug design must balance global drug properties with local structural determinants of target specificity. However, existing methods often reduce both objectives to local geometric optimization, relying on blind, reward-driven perturbations that can disrupt essential scaffolds and compromise overall drug-likeness. To resolve this destructive optimization trap, we propose CadreAI, a semantically decoupled agentic de novo drug design framework. CadreAI explicitly decomposes the entire drug design process into two independent subtasks: target-oriented semantic planning and plan-conditioned molecular generation. This strict separation mitigates potential task interference, allowing each module to focus exclusively on its dedicated objective without mutual disruption. Crucially, the strategic logic of how to formulate these target-oriented plans is driven by Simulation-Guided Insight Consolidation (SGIC). To eliminate trial-and-error guessing, this persistent memory mechanism translates transient numerical docking feedback into reusable textual heuristics, allowing the agent to continuously learn and logically deduce subsequent structural edits. Evaluated on the CrossDocked2020 and DrugGen benchmarks, molecules generated by CadreAI achieve superior docking performance with suitable drug-likeness and synthetic accessibility. Additional Boltz-2 evaluations provide orthogonal computational validation of predicted structural plausibility and binding affinity. These results demonstrate that semantically decoupled reasoning offers a highly controllable and practical route for in silico therapeutic design.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
abstract: Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra-low-power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI. Their breakthrough eliminates a long-standing "dead layer" problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin. Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials' electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities

title: Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of antibodies is often limited by the evolution of their targets. Designing or eliciting antibodies that withstand such evolution is challenging as their binding interfaces must accommodate antigenic variation. Here, we introduce Germinal Multi, a computational framework for de novo antibody design and rescue that jointly optimizes a single paratope against multiple antigenic variants. We applied Germinal Multi to cancer and viral antigens, targeting both observed antigenic variation and prospective antibody escape. Multi-target optimization yielded antibodies that bound resistance-associated EGFR variants or that neutralized antigenically distinct historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, with recognition extending to variants withheld from the design process. Beyond acting on observed evolution, we redesigned the broadly neutralizing antibody BD55-1205 to restore neutralization of a prospective escape variant engineered with guidance from an evolutionary forecasting model, while preserving activity against the parental variant. Successful candidates were identified after screening tens of designs per campaign. Together, these results establish multi-target computational design as a strategy for generating antibody breadth across observed antigenic variation and demonstrate the potential of evolutionary forecasting to guide antibody redesign against prospective escape.

title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
abstract: Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
abstract: The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic…

title: Predicting CO2 Reduction Selectivity on Large-Scale Cu–Pd Nanoparticles via a Multi-Scale Machine Learning Framework
abstract: The conventional computational approach to electrocatalyst evaluation has long been limited by its reliance on simplified slab models and adsorption energies on bare surfaces, which fail to capture the structural complexity of realistic nanoparticles (NPs) and the presence of adsorbates that decorates electrode surfaces under working conditions. To bridge this gap, we present a multi-scale computational framework that combines machine learning potential (MLP)-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with the explicit realization of potential-dependent surface coverage and high-throughput…

title: Conformationally Locked Yttrium Indanosalan Complexes for Fast Isoselective Ring-Opening Polymerization of β-Butyrolactone at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: We report rigid yttrium indanosalan complexes for the high-temperature ring-opening polymerization of β-butyrolactone. Some of the complexes (isolated or obtained in situ) developed were able to polymerize β-butyrolactone with high isoselectivity (Pm = 0.88) and very high activity (TOF up to 135,000 h–1) at a polymerization temperature of 100 °C, at which the polymer remains in solution, facilitating its further processing. Polymerization at 30–60 °C yielded the poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s with Pm up to 0.94.

title: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
abstract: Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity.

title: TDDFT Gradients and Nonadiabatic Couplings with Minimal Auxiliary Basis Set Approximation for Fewest-Switches Surface Hopping Dynamics
abstract: The electronic structure calculations remain a major bottleneck in ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics. We develop an efficient TDDFT-based FSSH implementation in the GPU4PySCF package for medium-sized molecular systems. Our approach combines density fitting, TDDFT with minimal auxiliary basis sets (TDDFT-ris), and an approximate Z-vector solver to reduce the computational cost of TDDFT excited states and derivative coupling calculations. These approximations introduce modest changes in the relaxation time scales while maintaining high computational efficiency.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Training reservoirs without looking back
A perfect couple: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis
abstract: They say opposites attract, and many couples do fit this pattern. One is pragmatic and down-to-earth, while the other is a dreamer with their head in the clouds. Yet, these differences make them perfect for each other. According to researchers at ICFO, chemical interactions between atoms are not that different. Ruthenium, for instance, belongs to the "dreamer" class. It is commonly used in single-atom catalysts that speed up water electrolysis, which splits water to obtain green hydrogen.
